## Summary

Asked whether I had researched current Rust features, and I had not — the MCP SDK tier was verified earlier but the language and tooling claims came from memory. Researched them and found two of my own objections were overstated, so corrected the artifact at ff9f4ee7. First, distribution: I claimed going native means losing npm, npx and the single-tarball property behind the Homebrew formula. Wrong. Native binaries ship through npm as per-platform optionalDependencies, and the proof was already in this repo's lockfile — TypeScript 7 distributes its native Go compiler as 20 platform packages, from typescript-darwin-arm64 through win32-x64, with npm resolving the matching one. npx keeps working and brew could still source the tarball. The real cost is 20 published artifacts plus cross-compile CI, a pipeline problem rather than a distribution dead end. Second, the library surface: napi-rs is production-mature, carrying swc, rolldown and lightningcss, so Node consumers of the engine and client entry points would survive a Rust core. Only the browser bundle genuinely has no answer short of WASM, so that objection half survives. Current Rust is 1.97 from July 2026 on edition 2024, with async closures, type alias impl Trait and the Polonius borrow checker as the notable recent additions; column header updated from the vague 1.0 since 2015. Verdict unchanged, and the reason is the point worth keeping: better Rust tooling lowers the cost of the port, it does not raise the benefit, which is still about 20ms of node boot on IO-bound work.
